The season commenced on 14 February and concluded on 21 May 2026. [[Mohun Bagan Super Giant|Mohun Bagan]] are the defending champions, having won their second [[Indian Super League]] title. [[East Bengal FC|East Bengal]] won their first ISL title and fourth overall [[List of Indian football champions|Indian title]], ending a 22-year league drought.{{Cite news |first=Debodinna |last=Chakraborty |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/football/story/east-bengal-indian-super-league-champions-mohun-bagan-final-day-2915187-2026-05-21 |title=East Bengal end 22-year drought with maiden ISL title, Mohun Bagan suffer front-row pain |date=21 May 2026 |work=India Today}} == Background == === Developments === * In June 2025, the [[Football Sports Development Limited|FSDL]] formally informed the ISL clubs and the [[All India Football Federation|AIFF]] that the 2025–26 season was on hold due to unresolved contractual issues, ahead of the expiry of the ''Master Rights Agreement'' in December.{{cite web|title=BREAKING: ISL 2025-26 season formally on hold; FSDL informs clubs & AIFF|date=11 July 2025|url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-isl-officially-on-hold-202507|website=Khel Now|access-date=11 July 2025}}{{cite web|title=With ISL on hold, AIFF enters new depths of incompetence|date=12 July 2025|url=https://www.espn.in/football/story/_/id/45718142/with-indian-super-league-isl-2025-26-hold-aiff-enters-new-depths-incompetence-football|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date=2 August 2025}} After the intervention of the Supreme Court of India, which requested both parties to resolve the issues between them and start the 2025–26 season as quickly as they could, both parties promised that the new season would start in December.{{Cite web|url=https://www.news9live.com/sports/football/isl-likely-to-begin-in-october-mra-negotiations-hinge-on-aiff-elections-2884498|title=ISL likely to begin in October; MRA negotiations hinge on AIFF elections|website=newsn9ne|date=26 August 2025|access-date=26 August 2025}}{{Cite web |date=2025-09-02 |title=Supreme Court paves way for ISL 2025/26 to start in December, no mention of fresh AIFF election |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/football/isl-2025-26-december-aiff-supreme-court-order-election-10226593/ |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} * The season was delayed even further after no bids came in for a tender for commercial partners floated by the AIFF on 16 October 2025.{{Cite web |date=2025-11-07 |title=ISL fails to attract single bid; AIFF to ‘deliberate on future course of action’ |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/indian-football/isl-no-bidder-aiff-official-statement-road-ahead-latest-news-updates/article70253845.ece|access-date=2025-11-08 |website=[[Sportstar]] |language=en}} * On 6 January 2026, after discussions with the stake holders, [[Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports|sports minister]] [[Mansukh Mandaviya]] confirmed that ISL would begin on 14 February, and would be played in a single leg home-and-away format for a total of 91 matches.{{Cite web |date=2025-11-07 |title=Impasse over, ISL to begin on 14 February with the participation of all 14 clubs |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/sports/football/impasse-over-isl-to-begin-from-feb-14-with-participation-of-all-clubs-3853287|access-date=2026-01-06 |website=[[Deccan Herald]] |language=en}} * On 12 January 2026, all 14 clubs confirmed their participation in this season. The AIFF outlined a total proposed budget of ₹24.26 crore for the season, a significant reduction from the previous seasons. The federation will contribute ₹9.77 crore upfront, while each participating club will provide ₹1 crore. The remaining expenses will be managed through allocated federation resources as the league progresses.{{Cite web |date=2026-01-12 |title=All clubs confirm participation for ISL 2025-26|url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-clubs-confirm-participation-isl-202601|access-date=2026-01-14 |website=Khel Now|language=en}} * The [[Asian Football Confederation]] granted India a one-season exemption from the mandatory 24-match league requirement. Hence, both the ISL champions and [[2025–26 AIFF Super Cup|Super Cup]] winners will be eligible to participate in the [[2026–27 AFC Champions League Two]] qualifiers next season.{{Cite web |date=2026-01-15 |title=AFC grants one-season exemption to India; ISL champions set to participate in ACL 2 qualifiers|url=https://khelnow.com/football/indian-football-isl-afc-grants-one-season-exemption-202601|access-date=2026-01-15 |website=Khel Now|language=en}}{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-04-24 |title=India spots restricted to Asian Champions League 2, despite increase in berths in ACL Elite |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/indian-football/india-spots-in-afc-asian-champions-league-2-2026-27-indian-super-league-news/article70902893.ece |access-date=2026-04-25 |website=Sportstar |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2026-01-15 |title= Shortened ISL gets AFC approval but Indian Clubs Lose Direct Entry to ACL2 Slots |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/shortened-isl-gets-afc-approval-but-indian-clubs-lose-direct-entry-to-acl-2-slots-what-it-means/articleshow/126545245.cms |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[The Times of India]] |language=en}} * Following a media rights tender by the AIFF in January 2026, OTT sports streaming platform [[FanCode]] were announced as winners of the broadcasting rights and will be the official streaming partner of the 2025–26 season, while KPS Studios won the bid for production rights.{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/fancode-awarded-isl-broadcast-rights-kps-studios-bag-production-rights/articleshow/127862323.cms|title=FanCode awarded ISL broadcast rights; KPS Studios bag production rights|date=2 February 2026|via=The Economic Times - The Times of India}} The Indian Super League (ISL) 2025–26 season will be broadcast on the [[Sony Sports Network]] after [[FanCode]] sublicensed the linear TV rights to the media conglomerate.{{Cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/isl/isl-news/where-to-watch-isl-2025-26-sony-sports-network-broadcast-rights-deal-indian-super-league-fancode-news/article70629887.ece|title=ISL 2025-26: Sony Sports to show Indian Super League on TV after FanCode sublicenses broadcasting rights|date=14 February 2026|via=Sportstar - The Hindu}} === Changes from last season === *This is the first season without the post-season [[Indian Super League playoffs|ISL Cup playoffs]].{{Cite web |first=Menon |last=Anirudh |url=https://www.espn.in/football/story/_/id/47917352/isl-2026-begins-indian-football-continuing-revel-absurd |title=ISL 2026 begins with Indian Football continuing to revel in the absurd |access-date=5 March 2026 |work=ESPN}} The 14 participating clubs will compete in a single-leg [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] format, with each team playing 13 matches. The table toppers at the end of the league will be crowned [[champions]].{{Cite web |title=ISL 2025-26 fixtures announced |url=https://www.the-aiff.com/article/isl-2025-26-fixtures-announced |website=the-aiff.com |access-date=4 March 2026 |publisher=All India Football Federation}} * The AIFF will implement [[Promotion and relegation|relegation]] this season onwards, despite objections from all 14 clubs, who cited the shortened season as their primary concern.{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/isl-for-first-time-bottom-ranked-club-set-for-relegation-to-second-division/articleshow/128321303.cms|title=ISL: For the first time, the bottom-ranked team is set for relegation|date=14 February 2026|via=[[The Times of India]]}} == Teams == 14 teams from 12 cities are competing in the 12th season of Indian Super League – thirteen from the previous season and one promoted from the [[2024–25 I-League|I-League]].
